tells.3: Uniformly polished three-part bullet pattern (label + full sentence + 'so you...' clause) is slightly templated
tells.4: Forced folksy register ('Maybe you're bouncing back', 'tweak your plan', 'keep you moving forward') reads like a deliberate casualness pass
tells.5: Vague filler 'get more of what the app has to offer' and the 'keep your recovery moving' cliché

reason: Version 2 has the slightly clunky, exclamation-marked voice of a real developer listing, but its subscription copy is awkward and less clear. Version 3 keeps the clarity and correct terms of the polished versions without their marketing filler, so it is the most credible to publish.
